summary: Feed s184_triple to IDS is degraded with 3 faults: 6.6% oversize jumbo frames (up to 8058B) dropped by 1518B IDS port, 3.0% TCP packet drops indicating visibility loss, and 10.2% duplicates. IDS is blind to ~9.6% of traffic due to drops/oversize and wastes cycles on duplicates, significantly reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Monitored network is forwarding jumbo frames (up to 8058 bytes) while IDS port MTU is 1518 bytes. Packet broker is forwarding them unchanged, so IDS NIC drops them at ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to 6.6% of frames (218/3309). Any attack or data exfiltration inside jumbo frames is missed; IDS cannot reassemble or inspect them, creating evasion opportunity and requiring full payload.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs full payload but cannot receive frames >1518B. Enabling 9000B jumbo MTU on IDS NIC/tool port (or having broker handle jumbos) prevents NIC-level drops without slicing payload needed for detection.

findings.root_cause: 95 of 3148 TCP packets show gaps/missing data (3.0%) indicating packets lost in visibility path. Most likely SPAN/mirror buffer overflow or oversubscribed broker ingress dropping under load; tool_overload is healthy so not tool-side overload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS TCP reassembly fails for 3% of packets, causing missed signatures, broken stream reconstruction, and false negatives for an IDS that requires both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Physical TAPs do not drop under load like SPAN buffers do, eliminating the 3% loss and ensuring complete TCP streams reach the IDS for reliable detection.

findings.root_cause: 10.2% duplicate packets (339/3309) indicates broker is aggregating the same traffic from multiple SPAN/TAP sources or both directions without deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes ~10% of its 1Gbps capacity processing duplicates, inflates flow/connection counts, skews analytics, and can cause false positives while masking true loss.

recommended_fix.why: Broker-side deduplication removes identical packets within a short window before delivery, freeing IDS cycles for unique traffic and restoring accurate detection without losing coverage.
